    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    But the overall-clad creator isn’t just helping tots reach their learning milestones online—she’s also advocating for children caught up in the U.S. immigration system.

    On Monday, Ms Rachel (aka Rachel Accurso) joined U.S. Representative-elect Brad Lander at an immigration court in New York City to support children expected to take part in legal hearings without attorneys.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Accurso posted a video of the visit on Instagram, where she wrote that “Kids representing themselves in immigration court is so wrong… I saw Angel up at the mic without a lawyer and I couldn’t believe it. He’s 9 years old! Hearing kids hear the word ‘removable’ over and over about themselves… Heartbreaking.”.

    A nine-year-old appearing in court without a lawyer may seem unfathomable, but Angel is far from the only child representing himself within a deeply complicated immigration system.

    Earlier this year, the Trump administration failed to renew a contract “with a nationwide network of legal service providers that represented thousands of unaccompanied minors in immigration court” (per the Times Union). While Governor Kathy Hochul announced state funding to combat the sudden gap in resources, Newly introduced York still has “the third-largest unaccompanied minors caseload in the nation” with nearly 10,000 open cases as of August 2026.

    As severe as Newly introduced York’s backlog is, it’s just one part of a nationwide crisis—and Accurso isn’t limiting her advocacy to the East Coast.

    Just a few days before appearing at the Ted Weiss Federal Building in NYC, the creator used her expansive online platform to spotlight a conversation with Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa. In a video shared on Instagram, Hinojosa shared her strategy to end family immigration detention—a cause Accurso herself has vocally championed.

    Advocacy on multiple fronts has long been a key part of Accurso’s online presence, despite repeated backlash from right-wing critics and parents over her support for the LGBTQ+ community and Palestinian children impacted by the war in Gaza.

    The creator’s contributions to the latter cause include a 2024 campaign that raised $50,000 for Save the Children’s Emergency Fund and, more recently, a $1 million pledge to the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund.

    Sources indicate that now, as Accurso fights for the rights of minors in U.S. courtrooms and detention centers, she’s demonstrating once again that all children are welcome in Ms Rachel’s classroom.

    #148311. Thumbnails help YouTubers build audiences. Now everyone can put custom ‘nails on their Shorts.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (478 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tubefilter ↗ Open Full Page

    Thumbnails help YouTubers build audiences. Now everyone can put custom ‘nails on their Shorts.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that you get a thumbnail.
    • That’s right: YouTube has, at long, long last, finally allowed all creators to assign customized thumbnails to their Shorts.
    • Sources indicate that when YouTube introduced Shorts in 2020, they were its attempt to keep up with TikTok.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that you get a thumbnail. And you get a thumbnail! And you . . .

    That’s right: YouTube has, at long, long last, finally allowed all creators to assign customized thumbnails to their Shorts.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Sources indicate that when YouTube introduced Shorts in 2020, they were its attempt to keep up with TikTok. TikTok didn’t offer custom thumbnails, because its whole platform is based on endless scrolling. The thought process was that if short-form videos did have thumbnails, people wouldn’t really see them, because videos are discovered by swiping up, not by visiting a creator’s profile.

    Recent findings suggest that but we all know that viewers do visit creators’ profiles. Not only do thumbnails–for long- or short-form–help a creator define their visual style and personal brand, but unique thumbnails help repeat viewers identify videos they’ve watched (and also, as a bonus plus, keep creators from being stuck with a perhaps unflattering moment as their content’s hero image).

    Sources indicate that tikTok later caved and added thumbnails to short-form videos. But YouTube, Land of Thumbnails, did not–at least, not until this past summer.

    In July, YouTube introduced custom Shorts thumbnails for everyone in the YouTube Partner Program, with YouTube CEO Neal Mohan saying custom thumbnails were “one of the most requested features” for the platform.

    You loved custom Shorts thumbnails—now every creator can use them on desktop and mobile!

    ✏️ Tap the pencil icon on any Short in @YouTube Studio to upload yours.

    — Neal Mohan (@nealmohan) November 23, 2026.

    YouTube’s thumbnail selection tool allowed creators to add their own images, just like with long-form videos, but also offers a TikTok-esque option where it’ll select a few screenshots from within the video and offer them as default thumbnails, for anyone who doesn’t want to apply YouTube-effort editing to their short-form content.

    It has been revealed that there’s one important thing to note from the July announcement, though: Shorts thumbnails went out to all YouTube Partner Program creators. Not to everyone–including any creators who are trying to drum up enough viewership to become a Partner creator.

    Sources indicate that this is a significant flip from 2024, when YouTube outright said it didn’t think Shorts thumbnails could be as impactful as long-form thumbnails. And, look, we get it: Shorts thumbnails vs long-form thumbnails is sort of like putting a half-page up against a full spread, to put things in publication terms. Shorts thumbnails inherently offer less room to work with, and thus less room to communicate videos’ vibes.

    But half-pages are still important in the grand scheme, and considering how much watch time Shorts drives for YouTube and for creators, they should have the same audience engagement and brand identity tools as long-form content.

Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

    Most product designers want to design for everyone. This role is for someone who'd rather design for one very specific, very opinionated person: the developer at 2am trying to figure out why their voice agent just failed a call. You'll design the tools developers use to test, evaluate and debug AI agents — a category that's still being invented, with no established patterns to copy. If dense data, real-time systems and reading a stack trace sound more fun than intimidating, keep reading.

    You'll thrive as a Senior Product Designer if you:.

    are obsessed with making the best product for our customers.

    are known as the go-to person for tackling tough problems.

    work hard and can build and ship fast.

    are focused on polish, detail and quality.

    are a fast learner, frequently picking up latest tips, tricks, and skills.

    The best way to impress us is with thoughtful ways you'd implement LiveKit, and potentially tinkering with it 😊.

    Own the design of how developers test, evaluate and observe their agents — simulations, evals, logs and agent insights.

    Turn complex, real-time data into interfaces that are easy to scan, understand and act on.

    Design newly introduced interaction patterns for AI-native workflows, where agents generate the first draft and humans adjust it.

    Prototype in code and work hand-in-hand with engineers to ship polished work.

    Contribute patterns to our design system for dense, debugging-oriented surfaces.

    You've shipped design work for developer tools, observability or data-heavy products.

    You have strong data-visualization instincts and know when a chart beats a table (and when it doesn't).

    You're comfortable in code — reading PRs, tweaking Tailwind, building prototypes.

    You earn the trust of deeply technical customers and engineers.

    Experience designing for AI or agent tooling.

    AI tools are already a core part of how you design.

    An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

    Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers.

    Competitive salary and equity package.

    Health, dental, and vision benefits.

    Recent findings suggest that liveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@livekit.io.

    The #46 channel in this week’s Global Top 50 is getting even more eyeballs, thanks to one of its stars landing a role in a massive-screen film.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    According to recent reports, during this new media gold rush sparked by movies like Iron Lung, Obsession, and Backrooms, everyone’s been talking about Hollywood tapping creators to write, direct, and star in projects. But this isn’t just happening in the West.

    Sources indicate that indru, one of the youngest members of the vlog 4u family, was plucked up to feature during childhood scenes in the action/crime drama film Bachelor Party D’eux. A Nov. 19 vlog from the family has them trucking to the theater to watch the film’s opening day debut, and talking about how proud they are to have Indru make his first silver screen appearance. His total runtime in the film is around five minutes, right at D’eux‘s beginning, but he was on set for 10 days, Indru’s father explains.

    “It’s a massive dream come true,” he adds. “It’s a day we’ve been wishing for, waiting for, and dreaming about for a long time.”.

    Industry observers note that the family’s vlogs about Indru’s appearance have brought around ~140,000 views apiece–so not as much as their Tom and Jerry skits, which tend to earn tens of millions of views. This view discrepancy is pretty normal: When a channel has built an audience on one type of content with one subject, and then switches abruptly to posting something different, the new content can be hit-or-miss with viewers.

    But 140,000 views is nothing to sneeze at, and Indru’s movie vlogs getting that many eyes means at least a portion of the vlog 4u audience is interested in following his onscreen adventure (or adventures?).

    Recent findings suggest that what’s intriguing about this story is the vlog 4u channel’s growth in 2026, which very likely played a part in Indru being selected for his role. At the beginning of this year, the channel was bringing around 330 million views per month (again, nothing to sneeze at). It started seriously climbing in March 2026 (~700 million), and by August had crossed over one billion views a month. Now it’s getting 400 million weekly–a level of traffic that’s keeping it firmly in our top 50.

    Industry observers note that will this lead to Indru–or other vlog 4u members–starring in more films? Maybe! We’ve seen some YouTubers produce or star in megahits, while others’ attempts to theater-ize have not gone so well. Whichever way it goes for the vlog 4u family, they clearly won’t be hurting for audience engagement.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Clerk is on a mission to solve user management once and for all.
    • Our Dashboard is a primary tool for configuring our components, as well as a centralized place for managing your app’s users.
    • You’ll join Visual Designers, UI Engineers, and fellow Product Designers on the Clerk Design team to build our core product, the Clerk Dashboard.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Clerk is on a mission to solve user management once and for all. We are a globally distributed team dedicated to providing best-in-class developer experience, with obsessive attention to every detail. Today, we provide developers with full-stack React components and hooks like , , , useUser, and useOrganization. These APIs allow developers to build hard-to-get-right user and organization management flows. We believe that a component is worth a thousand APIs.

    Our Dashboard is a primary tool for configuring our components, as well as a centralized place for managing your app’s users.

    You’ll join Visual Designers, UI Engineers, and fellow Product Designers on the Clerk Design team to build our core product, the Clerk Dashboard. You’ll always keep developer experience first as you gain a deeper understanding of the business needs of user management. You’ll optimize for customer delight, flexibility, and ease-of-use within a complicated, technical domain.

    Collaborate with teammates to design new features. You’ll work closely with Product, Design, and Engineering across project lifecycles from ideation to implementation.

    Gather requirements. You’ll research the technology and customer impetus behind the features we release. You’ll attain a deep understanding of the problems we solve.

    Structure and prototype. You’ll create flows and interactions that make sense of complex information, whether it’s a static component or a multi-page view.

    Not settle for less than pixel-perfection. You’ll work with a world-class UI Engineering team to bring your Figma frames to life. You set the bar for quality.

    Elevate our design culture. You’ll support and expand the Clerk Design visual language, component library, accessibility practices, design system, and design processes.

    You’re a Senior(+) level Product Designer with experience working in authentication, user management, or developer tools. You love your craft. You push Engineers to build experiences they’re unsure if they’re capable of (and you expect them to do the same for you).

    You’re in the Americas. The Clerk Design team is spread across the globe; Product Design currently spans UTC+1 to UTC+5:30. You live in a location that is ±3 hours within U.S. Mountain Time (MDT, UTC−06:00).

    Recent findings suggest that you have technical fluency. You have a deep understanding of designing interactive software on the web. You don’t need to author production-ready front-end code, but it’s a massive plus if you can.

    According to recent reports, you work iteratively. Your process embodies a “ship and iterate” mentality. You value the quick pace of a growing startup like Clerk.

    You own your time. You’re a self-starter who would rather find a tough problem to solve instead of waiting for a fresh task. To be successful at Clerk, you need to make the most of the autonomy you’re given.

    In a recent development, 💰 Competitive Salary – We want you to know that we value the skills and experience you bring to the table. We go out of our way to make sure that you feel fairly compensated.

    📈 Equity Ownership – At Clerk, we believe in shared success. That's why we offer a stock option blueprint so that everyone can benefit from the growth and prosperity of the company.

    ⚕️ Health Coverage – We care about your well-being. That's why we offer top-tier health insurance to ensure that your health needs are fully met.

    Recent findings suggest that 🎧 Work Gear - Set up your ideal home office with the gear of your choice. At Clerk, we want to ensure that you have everything you need to perform at your best.

    According to recent reports, 🏖️ Flexible Vacation Policy – We believe in work-life balance and trust you to take the time you need. Although we recommend 25 days per year, our vacation policy is unlimited. This is in addition to observing national holidays specific to your country of residence.

    It has been revealed that 🌍 Diverse and Inclusive Team – Join our exceptional, diverse, and globally distributed team at Clerk. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute their best in building impactful products and tools for the modern web.

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Tubefilter ↗ Open Full Page

    On OnlyFans, one-time transactions are winning out over subscriptions

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Back in August, OnlyFans declared that 5,076 creators have brought in at least $1 million each since the NSFW hub kicked off in 2016, with total creator payouts adding up to $30 billion.
    • That last figure represents a solid increase in how much creators are making on OnlyFans—but the way they’re making money on the platform has evolved in recent years, too.
    • According to a recent report from Giggster, the vast majority of the $6.2 billion paid to OnlyFans creators in 2025 stemmed from non-subscription-based transactions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Back in August, OnlyFans declared that 5,076 creators have brought in at least $1 million each since the NSFW hub kicked off in 2016, with total creator payouts adding up to $30 billion. About 20% of that $30 billion—roughly $6.2 billion—was delivered to creators during the year that ended on November 30, 2025.

    That last figure represents a solid increase in how much creators are making on OnlyFans—but the way they’re making money on the platform has evolved in recent years, too.

    According to a recent report from Giggster, the vast majority of the $6.2 billion paid to OnlyFans creators in 2025 stemmed from non-subscription-based transactions. To compile its report (titled “Behind the OnlyFans Paycheck: Creator Payments, Platform Fees and U.S. Rankings”), the online marketplace combined “illustrative payment calculations with third-party estimates of OnlyFans creator accounts across all 50 states and Washington, D.C.” and examined “firm-level revenue by payment type and revenue attributed to the U.S.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    In a recent development, overall, the report estimated that 700,000 OnlyFans creator accounts are active in the U.S., a number that makes up roughly 28% of the platform’s global total. And despite representing less than 30% of OnlyFans accounts, Giggster found that ~62% of OnlyFans’ platform revenue ($965.4 million) was attributed to the U.S. in the 2025 fiscal year.

    One of the report’s most significant findings, however, relates to the rising importance of non-subscription-based revenue—aka payments from one-time transactions like tips, paywalled posts, paid direct messages, and custom content requests. According to Giggster, those payments generated 73% of OnlyFans’ platform revenue in the 2025 fiscal year (up from roughly 40% in 2020 and 60% in 2024).

    OnlyFans isn’t the only creator-driven platform leaning into one-time payments, either. In a 2024 end-of-year post, Patreon noted that creators on its platform “increased monthly revenue of one-time purchases by 4x” year-over-year. More recently, a study from Ipsos commissioned by TikTok predicted that over 60,000 U.S.-based TikTok LIVE creators would make “more than the median part-time monthly income” from gift earnings in 2025.

    Sources indicate that youTube has devoted significant resources to one-time transactions, too. In a January blog post, CEO Neal Mohan reassured creators that the video platform would “continue to invest” in “fan funding features like Jewels and gifts,” adding that “we know these are crucial revenue streams, especially outside the U.S., for creators like Santiago Matias, who uses Super Chat as a way for fans to influence the outcome of his hit reality series.”.

    At the end of the day, the rising importance of one-time transactions demonstrates an important truth for creators: if you want to earn more revenue, give fans more ways to pay you.

    Earlier this month, X rolled out a latest feature that allows people to clip moments from their favorite videos, add their own takes, and hit post without leaving the platform.

    In theory, that tool (inventively named “Clipping”) is a win-win for everyone involved. Clips credit and link back to the original videos, and both original creators and clippers can earn revenue through X’s engagement-based creator rewards program (aka Original Content Rewards).

    In a recent development, X isn’t stopping there, though. On November 20, the platform shared that “video is the fastest growing format on X,” adding that “Posts with video get 5x the reach and engagement, and 36% of all impressions now go to video.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Now, to build on that momentum, X has unveiled a fresh slate of video creation and streaming tools designed to help creators “produce polished vertical video without leaving” the platform. Those include….

    X is also beefing up monetization options for video creators. In addition to Original Content Rewards (which replaced the platform’s Revenue Sharing program earlier this fall), X has introduced Video Kickstart Bonus, “an invite-only pilot that pays creators a bonus for posting original vertical video under three minutes with no watermarks.”.

    Industry observers note that tikTok, of course, didn’t stay offline for very long—but that hasn’t stopped X from continuing to refine its video offerings. In February of this year, the platform rolled out a redesigned immersive player intended to make video more watchable on mobile.

    With its latest slate of video features and monetization options, X finally appears to be putting its money where its mouth is—and offering creators the tools they need to take advantage.

    Industry observers note that IShowSpeed, who’s #7 this week, also got a GTA VI boost. As one of YouTube’s top streamers and a video game enthusiast, he was basically 100% guaranteed to pivot his content and head to Vice City as soon as the game dropped.

    But he’s also doing a lot outside of GTA.

    2026 has been quite the year for Speed. Among recent accomplishments, he dropped an expansive, award-winning partnership with Expedia and landed the cover of LIFE Magazine for its 90th anniversary edition. Throughout the year, he regularly clocked between 50 and 100 million views per week–but in November, that number rose sharply, to almost 200 million a week.

    That’s because as busy as the rest of 2026 was, November has been especially busy. While GTA fervor built to an all-time high on the eve of its debut, Speed turned his attention elsewhere, and for good reason: He teamed up with former President and First Lady Barack and Michelle Obama to present The Eyes of Ghana, a feature-length documentary that follows 93-year-old cinematographer Chris Hesse as he “races against blindness and time to save over 1,000 films that reveal the hidden origin story of African independence.”.

    Directed by Oscar winner Ben Proudfoot and produced by the Obamas, the film went live on Speed’s YouTube channel Nov. 17, and has nearly 3 million views.

    Speed wasn’t done. His latest video features him racing against the man, the myth, the legend: Usain Bolt. Clocking in at 11 million views in only 48 hours, this upload is on track to be one of his biggest videos to date.

    Speed is going into 2027 with around ~500 million views a month–and considering his ambitious Obama and Usain partnerships, we can’t help wondering what substantial view-driver ideas he’ll bring home in the fresh year.

With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

    According to recent reports, camunda Hub is where enterprises run Camunda at scale. From Hub they manage their clusters and tenants, decide who can do what, and roll changes out across the whole organization. We’re looking for a Senior Product Builder to own the backend and architecture that let Hub manage a whole fleet of clusters. Your first focus will be the mechanism that sends access, secret, tenant and licence changes out to every connected cluster and brings deployments, health and audit records back. From there, you’ll shape Hub’s foundations: its event model, the service boundaries and data model other teams build on, and how Hub behaves when things fail or get upgraded. The platform is your product. Your users are platform administrators, Centres of Excellence and the builders across Camunda who depend on what you create. You’ll join a newly introduced two-person pod in our remote-first team. You’ll have real ownership as the person who makes the call, and you’ll build AI-first, from written specs through to production. Our customers run mission-critical processes on Camunda, so your work will matter to them every day.

    Take over Hub's fleet propagation mechanism from the team building its first version, and make it work for access, secrets, tenants, licences and custom roles.

    Write short design documents for foundational changes, get them reviewed by the teams that depend on them, and turn them into tested, shipped code.

    Design how Hub behaves when things go wrong: offline clusters, partial failures, Hub outages, and clusters being adopted or detached.

    Build the path from clusters back to Hub, starting with deployment inventory, health, audit records and licence status.

    Design Hub's first event and webhook mechanism, so admins and agents can react to changes instead of polling for them.

    Join the pod's rotations and Hub on-call, and help other builders take on backend work through reviews, guidelines and contract tests.

    What You Will Bring to the Role:.

    Experience building and running backend systems in production that other teams or customers depend on.

    Comfort taking a problem nobody owns yet and turning it into a design, a initiative and shipped code.

    Product judgment for technical users: you talk to the people who use your APIs and make trade-offs on their behalf.

    Clear, short writing that lets a remote team review and decide asynchronously.

    Care for how a system behaves when parts of it fail, not only for the happy path.

    It has been revealed that designed and shipped a control plane or similar system that pushes desired state to many targets. Knows outbox or event-log patterns, idempotent apply, versioning, retries and drift reconciliation.

    Senior backend engineering in Java (API design, relational data models, multi-tenant SaaS services) and hands-on Helm and Kubernetes for self-managed installations.

    Sources indicate that software architecture and failure analysis: partial failure, blast radius, consistency trade-offs. Has debugged production incidents in a distributed system and is ready for on-call.

    Sources indicate that has shaped an API or platform as a product, and writes design docs other teams can build on. Gets agreement across teams without formal authority.

    Builds AI-first from written specifications and checks AI output as carefully as any other code.

    Kubernetes operators or GitOps tools, for example Argo CD.

    OIDC, SCIM and permission models, or secret managers and licence systems.

    Camunda 8 or another workflow or orchestration engine.

    Enough frontend skill to build a thin UI on top of a backend capability.

    This role is an existing vacancy.

    #148278. Everyone wants a piece of creator IPs. Outshine Talent founder Barbara Jones is making that work in her clients’ favor.

    Everyone wants a piece of creator IPs. Outshine Talent founder Barbara Jones is making that work in her clients’ favor.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Creator IPs have been the talk of the town this year, and we don’t expect that to change as we head into 2027.
    • While much of the attention around this new media “gold rush” has focused on mainstream entertainment companies (finally) recognizing creators’ value, we think it’s equally as notable to spotlight development efforts happening within established creator-space companies.
    • Recent findings suggest that that’s why we chatted with Barbara Jones, who founded Outshine Talent in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Creator IPs have been the talk of the town this year, and we don’t expect that to change as we head into 2027. As you’ll know if you’re a regular Tubefilter reader, there are many creator IP projects in the works–some with major Hollywood studios, some with Netflix and Disney, some with smaller independent studios, and some produced entirely by creators themselves (maybe with a little help from YouTube?).

    While much of the attention around this new media “gold rush” has focused on mainstream entertainment companies (finally) recognizing creators’ value, we think it’s equally as notable to spotlight development efforts happening within established creator-space companies.

    Recent findings suggest that that’s why we chatted with Barbara Jones, who founded Outshine Talent in 2019. Prior to launching Outshine, Jones founded influencer marketing agency Intuition Media Group, where she spent 12 years, and also served as a founding board member of the Influencer Marketing Association.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    According to recent reports, jones recently expanded Outshine to a new arm, called Outshine Entertainment, that focuses on helping creators build original IPs across things like short films, microdramas, full-length films, and TV; it also produces live events. Outshine is encouraging its clients to take creative chances and make their dream projects, and is also encouraging studios and streamers that could offer financial and production support for those projects to get involved.

    Some of Outshine Entertainment’s current and prospective creator projects include:.

    In a recent development, “It’s a natural evolution for a lot of these creators to say, ‘I want to do more,'” Jones says. “‘I’m a great writer, I’m a comedian, I’m an actor, I want to do more of these things.’ And I feel the industry is actually realizing the value and saying, ‘Yeah, I think you’re right. We need to start supporting these upcoming, fresh faces, fresh ideas, things that are maybe a little more inexpensive and worth taking a shot on, seeing what we can do.'”.

    Sources indicate that jones says she feels the atmosphere right now is ripe for creators to experiment, and to license out their production ideas to places like Tubi that are willing to take the ride with them. She believes creators keeping a relatively low production cost will spur companies to support them.

    “We’re filling the pipeline with originals and new ideas and things that don’t have to cost a fortune to try and test,” she claims. “Creators have that ability to test things out, see where they go, and then expand upon them if something’s really, really going.”.

    She points to the Romano Brothers series as an example. Sahid, Maystrik, and Hernandez originally created the series as a parody of popular love sibling-rivalry love triangles in shows like The Summer I Turned Pretty. They weren’t sure it would take off, but they threw it up on TikTok–and after a very enthusiastic reception from viewers, they committed to the idea and turned it into a full-fledged original series with Tubi.

    Successful creators tend to be inherently good at identifying what content resonates with their viewers, and how to build on that content’s themes and ideas to widen the scope and keep people coming back. That’s exactly what happened with Never Have I Ever Spent the Winter with the Romano Brothers.

    Sources indicate that “They had just done it for themselves,” Jones says. “But they realized it would turn into something because it had audience interest. And that’s the fun part about it. I always say to our talent: The gatekeepers are gone. You’ve just got to try it. Just make it. We can always find money. We can find resources. We can find those things, but everyone’s looking for fresh ideas, for ingenuity.”.

    She points to another plus of working with creators: They’re “speedboats” whereas traditional entertainment tends to be a “cruise ship.”.

    With creators, “You can be quicker to try things,” she claims. “And, for the first time, I’m really feeling like there are outside forces that want to help creators fund some of these things.”.

    With that funding in hand, creators are “leveling up, because now these are productions versus being solo, making everything yourself,” Jones indicates.

    Some funding can come from brands, Jones thinks. “I was just talking to a brand at one of our events, and I was saying, Why aren’t we just doing a microdrama? Let’s just do a microdrama that has product placement in it, but is actually a fun storyline,” she says. “That takes a normal sponsored post to the next level. We have to start thinking differently. I really believe creators are modern media, and I think people are catching up to that and realizing [a creator’s] audience is what they need to be focused on.”.

    According to recent reports, we’ve already seen a few brands push in and build their own microdramas to advertise products. It’s not far-fetched at all to envision a world where Sahid, Maystrik, and Hernandez’s next parody project comes with a sponsor–maybe even one that’s willing to be a little self-aware and play along with the satire. Imagine a classic romcom “oh no, there’s only one bed and it’s snowing outside so we have to cuddle!” situation sponsored by a cozy sleepwear firm, or a hot cocoa brand.

    Jones notes supporting creators’ original IPs is a top priority for Outshine going into 2027.

    It has been revealed that “It’s very exciting. I have a lot of young, fresh faces who are super creative and love to have ideas, and now I feel like I actually have places to bring them,” she states. “I have people who are really listening to what creators can do.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    Recent findings suggest that we’re looking for a Software Engineer, AI Tooling Infrastructure to join our AI Tooling team and help build and run the backend services behind Supabase’s AI products. The Supabase MCP server is one example of what the team runs in production, alongside the services that support agent skills and the dashboard assistant. You’ll work closely with the Platform, SRE, Auth, Billing and Edge Functions teams, and with the engineers on the AI Tooling team who build the product surfaces.

    According to recent reports, the AI Tooling team runs its own services in production and carries its own on-call. Traffic from AI clients and agents behaves differently from traffic from people: hundreds of calls a minute, retry loops, and no reading of deprecation warnings. This role makes sure the services they use are reliable, correctly authorized and observable. It is a systems and infrastructure role rather than a product AI role, and it is not an SRE role. You will build and operate these systems, not only advise on them.

    This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments, owns what they ship in production, and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

    Build and operate the production backend services behind Supabase’s AI products, including the MCP server: deployment, scaling, configuration and release.

    Take ownership of how those services are structured, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

    Define, measure and meet reliability targets for the services the team runs. Set SLOs with the SRE team, track error budgets, and use them to decide what to fix first.

    Participate in the AI Tooling team on-call rotation, and be a first responder for incidents in those services. Investigate, fix, coordinate with other teams during incidents, and write the follow-ups and runbooks.

    Work the AI Tooling team support queue alongside on-call, and turn recurring issues into fixes rather than repeated manual answers.

    Own authentication and authorization for AI and agent clients: OAuth apps, scoped tokens, and permissions that make sense for agents as well as humans, including how we change or deprecate a permission without breaking existing integrations.

    Own observability for the services the team runs: metrics, traces, logs, dashboards and alerts, so we find problems before customers do.

    Handle capacity and abuse for agent traffic: rate limits, cost and safety controls, and behavior under load or when a dependency degrades.

    Improve the architecture of the services the team owns as they grow, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

    Work with the Platform team on shared code, review ownership and release process, and with the SRE team on infrastructure, alerting and incident practice.

    Contribute to the code of the AI Tooling team’s tools, such as the MCP server, where it affects reliability and security, in partnership with the engineers who own the product surface.

    Have 5+ years of experience building and running backend services in production, and have carried on-call for them.

    Write strong TypeScript or Go, and are comfortable working in the other.

    Have designed and operated APIs with real consumers: versioning, error handling, rate limiting, and backwards-compatible change.

    Know OAuth, OIDC, JWT and API authorization well enough to debug them in production and to explain where implementations commonly deviate from the spec.

    Have a good understanding of PostgreSQL and relational databases.

    Industry observers note that are comfortable with CI/CD, Docker and containerized deployments, and with infrastructure as code. Any tool is fine.

    Can debug across services: follow a slow or failing request through several systems using metrics, traces and logs.

    Communicate clearly in writing, work with a wide range of stakeholders, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving promptly.

    Pick your centre of gravity. We expect you to be deep in at least one of these, and to tell us which:.

    APIs and auth: You have designed permission models, token scopes or OAuth flows for third-party or machine clients, and you have migrated them without breaking people.

    Operations: You have run production services yourself: carried the pager, written alerts and runbooks, used SLOs or similar to decide what to fix, and made shared systems less risky over time.

    Gateways and distributed systems: You have built or run proxies or gateways, or debugged hard failures across services (retries, partial failures, upstream outages, fail-open vs fail-closed decisions), and you can reason about load and degradation.

    Experience with agent tooling (MCP or similar), or serving traffic from AI agents and LLM clients.

    Experience moving a service out of a larger codebase while keeping existing clients working.

    Experience with Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Logflare or a similar observability stack, and real SLO work.

    Open-source contributions, especially to Node.js, Go, TypeScript or API tooling.

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the organization. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    According to recent reports, supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are vital to us.

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a upcoming city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    In a recent development, we operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    In a recent development, supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    In a recent development, we move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google published new guidance on how to keep from blocking its user-triggered AI agents that identify themselves as Google-Agent.
    • It has been revealed that google’s newly introduced guidance on Google-Agent may be related to its announcement of the expansion of Personal Intelligence, which came after this article was originally published.
    • Personal Intelligence enables Google to draw on information from across its products and services to better understand what users want to accomplish and provide increasingly personalized assistance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google published new guidance on how to keep from blocking its user-triggered AI agents that identify themselves as Google-Agent. The new documentation shows how to verify legitimate Google-Agent requests and configure firewalls to allow them on websites.

    It has been revealed that google’s newly introduced guidance on Google-Agent may be related to its announcement of the expansion of Personal Intelligence, which came after this article was originally published. Both developments are consistent with Google CEO Sundar Pichai’s description of a unified experience across Google’s products and services that’s mediated by an agentic layer.

    Personal Intelligence enables Google to draw on information from across its products and services to better understand what users want to accomplish and provide increasingly personalized assistance.

    Google’s announcement offers an example of how this works:.

    “So if you’ve been researching and planning for a trip, you can pick up right where you left off in a new search thread without starting over or repeating yourself.”.

    Planning a trip can involve researching destinations, comparing accommodations, and making reservations. That’s precisely the kind of task-based search where user-triggered AI agents may fetch information from websites, interact with them, and complete tasks on behalf of consumers.

    What makes the timing of Google’s Google-Agent guidance interesting is that Google is simultaneously expanding its ability to understand what customers want to accomplish and publishing guidance for website owners on how to make sure that user-triggered AI agents are not blocked from accessing websites.

    Although Google has not explicitly connected Google-Agent to Personal Intelligence, the two developments appear to complement each other in terms of Google’s larger goal of creating a personalized, task-based Search experience.

    It has been revealed that google-Agent is the name used by AI agents hosted on Google’s infrastructure that navigate websites and perform actions on behalf of users. Google’s guidance and also Google’s User-Triggered Fetcher documentation do not identify which Google products or services use Google-Agent. Neither documentation mentions Google Search, AI Mode, Gemini, or any other Google product.

    It describes Google-Agent as agents that are hosted on Google’s infrastructure, interact with and navigate websites, and complete tasks on behalf of a user.

    The document indicates or implies that the Google-Agent does the following:.

    The new guidance explains there are three ways that website owners can verify that a request comes from Google-Agent.

    In a recent development, 1. The request’s User-Agent header contains “Google-Agent.”.

    According to recent reports, 2. The request originates from an IP address listed in Google’s published file of user-triggered agent ranges.

    According to recent reports, 3. Only where it’s present, when the request carries a cryptographic signature under Google’s experimental Web Bot Auth protocol, which can be checked against Google’s published public keys.

    Industry observers note that the first two checks are the baseline, and the signature check adds stronger verification when it’s available. A Google-Agent bot can then be allowed through whatever bot defenses are in use once it passes those checks. Google also notes that some CDNs and bot-detection services handle this verification automatically.

    Lastly, Google offers guidance on troubleshooting when the Google-Agent is unintentionally blocked.

    Google recommends ensuring that rules allowing Google-Agent requests have higher priority and are evaluated before broader blocking rules, including:.

    If bot detection, firewall (WAF), or CDN rules only covers the initial page request, the agent will be able to land on the website but it will be unable to finish whatever task it’s there to accomplish.

    Google recommends checking that CAPTCHA challenges are disabled for verified Google-Agent requests, reviewing rate limits, IP address updates, and proxy configurations.

    “Proxy headers: Confirm that load balancers and intermediate proxies preserve the original client IP, the User-Agent header, and (for signed requests) the Signature, Signature-Input, and Signature-Agent headers.”.

    Google’s latest guidance addresses three issues to check if Google-Agent is being inadvertently blocked:.

    “Shared-IP rate limits: Confirm that per-IP rate-limiting rules account for or exempt verified Google-Agent IP ranges, as concurrent requests from multiple consumers share the same egress pool.

    IP range updates: Confirm that IP-based rules stay synced with the latest ranges in user-triggered-agents.json.

    Proxy headers: Confirm that load balancers and intermediate proxies preserve the original client IP, the User-Agent header, and (for signed requests) the Signature, Signature-Input, and Signature-Agent headers.”.

    Google’s latest Google-Agent guidance offers tips for website owners who want to allow Google-Agent interactions, stressing that they need to make sure that legitimate Google-Agent requests can pass through security defenses without compromising protections against unwanted bots.

    Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.About the Role.

    We’re looking for a Product Manager, Administration & Governance to join our Product Team and make Supabase the default starting point for software built inside a company.

    It has been revealed that supabase already spreads from the bottom up: someone has an idea, creates a project, and builds something useful. Inside most companies, Supabase starts the same way: someone has an idea, creates a project, and builds something useful. The next step is making that momentum company-wide: one platform where anyone can start building, and where IT can see what’s running, who owns it, and what it costs.

    According to recent reports, you’ll own how companies run Supabase as their internal development platform: approved by IT and easy for anyone in the firm to use. You’ll make it possible for people and the agents they work with to start building without waiting on infrastructure, while giving platform, IT, and security teams the controls they need to say yes. The goal is to make the approved path the easiest path, from an early experiment to a production application, with the controls companies need built in.

    Own the product strategy and roadmap for internal innovation, from a organization’s first IT-approved rollout to adoption across teams and business units.

    Recent findings suggest that make getting started self-service, whether someone creates a project in Supabase, through an internal developer portal, or with an agent. Give builders the access and infrastructure they need without a ticket for every project.

    Steer scattered usage into a manageable manufacturer-wide platform. Give companies one view of everything they run on Supabase. Shape how ownership, delegated access, and boundaries work so teams can move independently as usage grows.

    Sources indicate that partner closely with platform, IT, security, and finance teams to understand what it takes to approve Supabase and keep it approved. Translate their needs into practical identity, policy, audit, and spend controls that don’t slow builders down.

    Define the path from experiment to production, including project ownership, access, and the guardrails that change as an application becomes vital to the business.

    Work with Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success to turn early customer rollouts into a repeatable experience, rather than a fresh custom integration for every company.

    Define what success looks like, instrument it end to end, and let the data guide what gets built next—from time to first project and self-service adoption to production usage and expansion across the firm.

    Have 7+ years of product management on developer tools, infrastructure, or internal developer platforms.

    Have built self-service products that developers love and platform or IT teams trust. You understand both the person trying to ship an app and the team responsible for how it runs.

    Can reason about identity, permissions, organization boundaries, and usage attribution, and turn those systems into workflows people can actually understand.

    Have a strong point of view on how agents change who can build software inside a company and what an internal development platform needs to make that possible.

    Know your way around controlled experimentation and data analysis, and can connect easier adoption to sustained product use.

    Are biased toward speed and would rather ship, learn, and iterate than perfect a spec.

    Build with what you own and form opinions through first-hand use, from creating a project to configuring the policies around it.

    Use AI tools to compress research, drafting, and feedback synthesis so you can focus on judgment calls.

    Work async by default, making decisions in writing in a fully remote team.

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    It has been revealed that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are crucial to us.

    Once a year, the entire manufacturer gathers in a fresh city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Recent findings suggest that supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    In a recent development, we move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Your Black Friday advertising should now be built, paced, and approved. The useful work left is checking what’s running will continue running and being honest about anything that isn’t ready. Some of it can still be fixed in the few days before Black Friday on Nov. 27, and some of it belongs on next year’s strategy.

    Industry observers note that this is the checklist our team works through on the accounts we run through the end of the holiday season. Most of this is dull stuff, sure, but the last thing you want is something like this breaking at the worst possible time. So think of it like our checklist being passed on to you to make sure that doesn’t happen.

    If you have not built campaigns by now, you are really cutting it close and leaving it for last minute. For the accounts we run, the freeze date was last Friday, Nov. 20, and since then the only changes going in are fixes or tweaks. Any major changes now could trigger you right back into learning mode, and you don’t want that. Campaigns should be structured, stable, and running leading into Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM).

    It has been revealed that if something still isn’t built, only launch low-risk pieces, like a brand campaign if you somehow don’t have one, or promo creative inside an asset group or ad set that already has history. Anything structural goes on next year’s initiative.

    Pacing should have started in early November, so budgets are already close to where you want them on Black Friday instead of sitting at an October level waiting for one big jump on Thursday. Frankly speaking, most companies start their BFCM offers early, so if that’s you, you have nothing to worry about here because you might already be ramped up.

    On Meta, the ramp should have happened in steps, since frequent budget changes can send ad sets back into learning. Meta’s developer documentation describes budget scheduling as a way to “schedule budget increases for your campaign or ad set budget” for days when you expect higher sales. If you scheduled increases, check the dates and amounts against your sale.

    On Google, a campaign can spend up to twice its average daily budget on a given day, and no more than 30.4 times the average daily budget over the month. When you change a budget partway through the month, Google recalculates the monthly limit as what you’ve spent so far plus the upcoming daily budget times the remaining calendar days, counting the day of the edit.

    According to recent reports, cyber Monday 2026 falls on Nov. 30, the last day of the month, so if you raise a budget that morning, the monthly limit becomes what you’ve spent plus one day of the fresh budget, and you won’t be charged for more than that one day regardless of the 2x daily allowance. A campaign that runs close to double its budget Friday through Sunday is also using the monthly room Cyber Monday would have had. So treat Black Friday through Cyber Monday as one stretch, set those budgets before the weekend, and check on Sunday night how much monthly room your key campaigns have left.

    Google’s campaign total budgets let you set one budget for a three- to 90-day window on Performance Max, Search, and Shopping, but they’re only available for new campaigns, so this isn’t the week to start using them. The monthly limit starts over on Dec. 1, so set December budgets now as well.

    If budgets haven’t ramped, raise Google budgets today, since the change takes effect immediately and the rest of the month paces to the fresh number. On Meta, start stepping budgets up today rather than all at once on Thursday night. And write down the budget you wish you’d had on November 1, because that’s where next year’s ramp starts.

    See also: Google Ads Channel Priorities Have Limits – What PMax Still Won’t Let You Split.

    A few things can’t be checked in a settings screen, so these are the questions I’d want an honest answer to before Thursday, and what I’d do if the answer is no.

    Recent findings suggest that prospecting funded in September and October is what pays during BFCM. In our accounts, upper-funnel spend takes roughly six to eight weeks to show up in revenue, which is why I argued that September was the last month to fund it. Your own lag depends on price point and how long people take to decide.

    Recent findings suggest that if the answer is no: Don’t launch cold prospecting this week, when in our accounts prospecting CPMs are at their highest of the year. Keep the prospecting you have on a flat budget through the week and let harvest campaigns take the extra money. Put the build on next year’s calendar for September, as a fixed budget rather than a percentage of whatever is left.

    Recent findings suggest that it should lean towards Bottom Of Funnel (BoFu). BFCM is when the demand you built in the fall turns into orders, so retargeting, brand search, and your existing customers are going to take a bigger share of spend than they do the rest of the year. During the holidays, those sales are worth buying. What matters is that it was a decision. Before the week starts, you should know roughly how much budget is going to people who already know you, how much stays on new customers, and what the floor is for prospecting so it doesn’t get raided the first time retargeting looks great on Friday morning.

    Keep in mind that during BFCM, your email, SMS, retargeting, and brand campaigns are often all reaching the same person for the same order, and each one will report it. So don’t move budget into retargeting just because its ROAS looks great on Black Friday. Check it against what the store is actually doing overall before you add more.

    You can see the split on both platforms. On Google, lifecycle goal reporting adds a “Latest vs. returning customers” segment to the Campaigns table on campaigns where the new customer acquisition goal is turned on, and on Meta, audience segments break sales campaign results into new, engaged, and existing customers once you’ve defined them in your ad account settings.

    If the answer is no: Decide it today. Write down the prospecting floor and the rough share for newly introduced versus existing customers through Cyber Monday, and look at the new versus returning numbers each morning so you’re adjusting against the initiative instead of against whichever campaign has the best ROAS that day.

    You should by now. Testing is what October is for, and BFCM is when you have winning creative you know you can put advertising dollars against. That matters most on Meta, where the creative is doing most of the targeting in Advantage+, so in our accounts, a proven concept with the offer added to it tends to beat a brand latest idea during holiday shopping. The offer can go on as an overlay, in the first few seconds of a video, or in the headline, without changing what made the ad work in the first place.

    In a recent development, if the answer is no: Look back at the last 60 to 90 days, pick the best performer on each platform by cost per purchase, and add the offer to that. Don’t run a creative test during the most expensive week of the year, because whatever wins under BFCM pricing won’t tell you much about January. Put an October testing window on next year’s plan, so you go into the holiday season with your winners already picked.

    Industry observers note that every date through December should have creative approved and paused: Black Friday, Cyber Monday, any Cyber Week extension, shipping deadlines, last-minute gifts and gift cards, and post-Christmas on Dec. 26.

    Google’s ad review page claims most ads are reviewed within one business day and “changes to your ad or assets restart the review process and may cause delays.” Meta’s Marketing API best practices say changes to creative or targeting trigger review and that an ad entering review while paused stays paused after approval.

    If the answer is no: Submit what’s missing today with final copy and schedule it with end dates, because Thanksgiving week is short on business days and a typo caught after approval means another trip through review.

    Industry observers note that place a real order with your promo code and follow it into Google Ads and Meta Events Manager. A tag check only confirms that something fired, and a checkout change made in November can alter the value your purchase event sends without stopping it from firing.

    Industry observers note that if something is off, it’s worth pulling a developer in before Wednesday. If tracking breaks during the week anyway, fix it and apply a data exclusion so the bidder doesn’t learn from the broken days. Cancel the test order afterward.

    It has been revealed that the site banner, landing page, sale price in your feed, Merchant Center promotions, and ad copy should all say the same thing, because a mismatch usually shows up as disapprovals the morning the sale starts. Merchant Center’s automatic item updates are on by default and correct prices from your landing pages, but Google claims they may not work for products whose price changes more than once a day.

    Push your own feed updates for any hourly doorbusters, run a purchase on the promo landing page from a phone the way a customer would, and name the person who opens Merchant Center diagnostics first thing Black Friday.

    Billing is the item most likely to stop every ad you have. Google says a declined payment can stop the account, and on monthly invoicing, once costs reach the account budget, “all ads in the account stop running.” On Meta, the ad account spend cap is a hard stop, and “when the amount is reached, all delivery stops.”.

    According to recent reports, raise the invoiced account budget to cover the higher spend through Nov. 30, reset any Meta spend cap, check the card on file, and give at least two people admin access on both platforms and Merchant Center, with two-step verification on devices they’ll have over the holiday.

    Several Google Ads features that add promotions or pick landing pages are on by default, so go through them before your own promotion goes live.

    Industry observers note that I wouldn’t switch all of this off on principle. Decide on each one during the holidays and note what you changed so you can revisit it in January.

    Sources indicate that your brand campaign should be fully funded through Cyber Monday, and even into December. Keep an eye on auction insights daily to see which competitors are bidding on your brand. I know I’m stating the obvious, but this is definitely not the time of the year to let a competitor steal a brand sale. Be defensive, buy your brand terms, and keep that impression share % high. Keeping brand in its own campaign, which I’ve argued for before, makes a “Limited By Budget” status obvious the morning it happens.

    On one premium brand we work with, several competitors were bidding on the brand name, and we’ve consistently managed brand spend throughout the year, but during holiday shopping times, we max out impression share %.

    According to recent reports, once the checks are done, the hardest part of Black Friday advertising is leaving the account alone and letting it run. Of course, make sure there is someone keeping an eye on it from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday and have a initiative in place for what can change. Does pacing increase at all? If so, what % increase is the cap? Should any creative be swapped out? Messaging?

    We keep that checklist pretty short: budgets on campaigns that are hitting target and fixes for tracking or disapprovals, and everything else waits until Dec. 1.

    Keep a running list throughout the week of anything you couldn’t fix, whether that’s prospecting you never built, creative you didn’t get to test, or the budget you wish you’d started with in early November. It’s the most useful thing you’ll have when you start planning next year’s holiday season, and it’s a lot easier to write down this week than to piece together in January, or even next year.

    Featured Image: Master1305/Shutterstock.

    Check that budgets have ramped, that tracking records the right value on a real promo order, that billing won’t stop your ads, and that your offer matches across site, feed, and ads. Campaigns and creative should already be built, so the week is for checks and fixes.

    Enough that your best campaigns aren’t capped on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, based on your own past results rather than a round number. With Cyber Monday on November 30, set Google budgets before the weekend, since a budget raised on the last day of the month only gets one day of room.

    Industry observers note that for this year, mostly yes. In our accounts, upper-funnel spend takes roughly six to eight weeks to show up in revenue, so prospecting debuted now is bought at peak prices and mostly pays out in January. Keep what you have running and proposal next year’s build for September.

    Industry observers note that no. Results from BFCM week don’t carry over well to the rest of the year, and an untested concept is an expensive bet at peak prices. Put the offer on proven creative and test in October.

    Recent findings suggest that yes. If competitors bid on your brand and you don’t, you can lose those sales to them. Keep brand in its own campaign with enough budget and check auction insights daily through Cyber Week.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that cloudLinux is the maker of Imunify360 — a suite of security products protecting millions of websites across the web hosting industry — and of CloudLinux OS, the operating system behind a large share of the world's shared hosting. To learn more about our tech giant and products, visit our websites: cloudlinux.com and imunify360.com. Alongside those established product lines we run a small innovation team whose job is to find and prove the next ones.

    We are looking for a Product Owner to lead that team: a small, senior, fully remote squad of engineers that takes upcoming product concepts from idea to a working MVP in customers' hands, then hands proven products to a product line and moves on to the next concept. You will be accountable for the pipeline of ideas, the speed and rigour with which they are tested, and the evidence behind every go / no-go recommendation.

    This is a hands-on lead role, not pure people management: roughly 50% discovery and leadership (customer conversations, scoping, prioritisation, coaching, reporting to the CPO) and 50% building (prototypes, spikes, design and code review, demo stands). You will not be the team's only builder, but you must be able to build a credible prototype yourself and hold a technical opinion about every part of it.

    In a recent development, you don't need to arrive as an expert in web hosting or security. If you have taken a product from nothing to its first paying customers before — as a founder, an early engineer, or the lead of an incubation team — and you get deep into unfamiliar technical territory fast, we will teach you the market.

    The innovation team sits across CloudLinux and Imunify and owns the product concepts that do not yet have a home in an established product line. Ideas come from customer conversations, industry events, telemetry across more than 80,000 servers and the CPO’s strategy; the team’s job is to turn them into something a customer will pay for within a quarter, using AI coding agents throughout.

    Prototyping and technical direction.

    Industry observers note that we evaluate engineers partly on how effectively they work with coding agents, and in the innovation team this is the main lever on speed. As the lead you model and coach it: prompt specificity, review quality on agent-generated code, context provision, iteration and error recovery, and end-to-end task completion. Expect to use agents to build prototypes, generate test corpora and draft customer-facing material.

    #148245. Google Indicates Back Button Hijacking Policy Covers Social Visits via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📖 Baca

    Google Indicates Back Button Hijacking Policy Covers Social Visits via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (451 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google’s back button hijacking policy applies whenever the hijacking happens in a browser, including on visits from social media rather than Google Search, according to an FAQ Google added to its spam policies today.
    • Ad platform code is still allowed, the FAQ says, and Google acts only on pages that show the hijacking.
    • Google’s Search Central changelog says the FAQ answers common questions it has received about the policy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google’s back button hijacking policy applies whenever the hijacking happens in a browser, including on visits from social media rather than Google Search, according to an FAQ Google added to its spam policies today.

    Ad platform code is still allowed, the FAQ says, and Google acts only on pages that show the hijacking.

    Google’s Search Central changelog says the FAQ answers common questions it has received about the policy. I covered the policy when Google confirmed it in April, with enforcement set to start June 15.

    In a recent development, one FAQ question asks whether the back button hijacking policy covers people who arrive from a non-Search channel, such as social media, and then can’t get back to where they came from. Google wrote:.

    “If back button hijacking happens when a user is browsing within a browser, then the policy applies.”.

    A separate answer states “Discover is a part of Google Search and our spam policies apply to Discover as well.” That answer covers Google’s spam policies in general, not only this one.

    For a website that opens an external app, which then keeps the user from getting back to the site, the FAQ notes “app navigation and ‘open in app’ behaviors are outside the scope of the back button hijacking policy.”.

    Google’s FAQ shows how the policy applies to visits in a browser and where external app navigation falls outside its scope.

    Google’s April announcement mentioned some back button hijacking “may originate from the site’s included libraries or advertising platform,” and asked sites to remove or turn off the code behind it.

    The FAQ asks whether Google is preventing sites from importing code hosted by advertising platforms. Google wrote:.

    “No, site owners can continue to work with advertising platforms and import code that they host. We only take action on pages that exhibit back button hijacking behavior.”.

    According to recent reports, A back button test that starts from a Google results page doesn’t cover every visit the hijacking policy applies to. Test pages that carry ad code by arriving from a social media link and pressing back, and repeat it from Discover when one of your pages highlights up there.

    Recent findings suggest that google’s answer on ad code lets you keep your ad partners. The thing to remove is the code or setting on a page that interferes with the back button, wherever it comes from.

    Sources indicate that google’s FAQ also indicates owners can report back button hijacking through its spam report form. Those reports go toward improving Google’s spam detection systems, which gives people who hit hijacking on a social or Discover visit a way to flag a site.

    Featured Image: Tetiana Yurchenko/Shutterstock.

    I Blind-Tested 3 Gemini Models On Real SEO Questions – Neon Won 5 Of 6 via @sejournal, @marie_haynes

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Over the last few months, I have been quietly building something I call Marie’s Brain – a private AI co-pilot grounded in my hand-curated Open Knowledge Format (OKF) library of Search and AI research.
    • Recently, I switched the tool over to Google’s upcoming Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.
    • Instead of guessing, I decided to run a real blind taste test – and threw Gemini 4 Neon into the mix too.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Over the last few months, I have been quietly building something I call Marie’s Brain – a private AI co-pilot grounded in my hand-curated Open Knowledge Format (OKF) library of Search and AI research.

    Recently, I switched the tool over to Google’s upcoming Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. After using it for a while, though, I had a nagging feeling: Is Hydrogen actually producing better answers than Gemini 3.8 Flash, or am I just assuming newer means better?

    Instead of guessing, I decided to run a real blind taste test – and threw Gemini 4 Neon into the mix too.

    You can actually try the exact same six-question blind test yourself here (columns A, B, and C are shuffled on every question, and there is a button at the top to reveal how I voted and the real token costs).

    The blind 3-way taste test interface: columns A, B, and C are shuffled on every SEO question, complete with clickable OKF concept pills. Try voting blind yourself here. Image Credit: Marie Haynes.

    Before I even finished reading the first round of blind outputs, one thing jumped out immediately: The answers were way too long.

    My Brain had been defaulting to Detailed mode with no word ceiling. When we checked the API logs, we discovered something wild: Gemini 4 Hydrogen was going into an over-eager research loop, reading an average of 21 OKF files per question, taking 68 seconds, writing 1,600-word essays, and costing $0.44 per prompt – actually more expensive per turn than Gemini 4 Neon!

    On top of that, some answers were dropping internal Google engineering jargon (like MAGIT and FastSearch) that a busy business owner does not need to wade through just to figure out why their clicks dropped.

    So before doing my real blind vote, I made three quick upgrades to how Marie’s Brain works:.

    Then we re-ran the exact same six real-world SEO and AI Search questions – covering AI Overviews and traffic drops, whether to delete or rewrite informational posts, Main Content on commercial buyer’s guides, pruning thin location pages, agent readiness and /llms.txt, and a realistic five-hour-a-week proposal that skips GEO distractions – across Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and Gemini 4 Neon.

    With the model names hidden and the columns randomized, I read all 18 answers and picked a winner on every prompt.

    When I hit reveal, the result wasn’t even close:.

    What stood out to me about Neon wasn’t that it had more facts – all three models pulled from the exact same OKF files. It was how it communicated. Neon’s answers felt more like a smart human thinking through a problem rather than a predictable AI response. I genuinely enjoyed reading them, and I immediately understood what they were trying to get across.

    Recent findings suggest that my revealed blind test results (5/6 for Gemini 4 Neon), real Gemini API token usage, and pace-adjusted monthly cost estimates per user. Image Credit: Marie Haynes.

    According to recent reports, of course, better answers only matter if the economics make sense. Here are the real numbers from our live Concise-mode runs (using real Gemini API usageMetadata, including thinking tokens, at conservative uncached list rates):.

    Note on Neon’s speed: That 70.8s average was skewed by one single 3.5-minute API queue spike during testing; typical Neon replies ran 18 to 40 seconds (with text streaming on screen as it writes).

    Industry observers note that at first glance, $191 vs. $93 per 1,000 prompts sounds like a big jump (about 10 cents extra per prompt). But when I mapped that against realistic full-month usage paces extrapolated from my early active owners, here is what the extra cost per user looks like:.

    And those are conservative uncached estimates. Because every turn references the same ~55,000-token OKF Master Index, Gemini 4 Neon’s implicit context caching discounts repeated input tokens across multi-turn chats, bringing real-world bills noticeably lower.

    Featured Image: Thefirst7/Shutterstock.
